decisions.question: Should common config files (pyproject.toml, package.json, Makefile, tsconfig.json, etc.) be implicitly allowed for all implement-phase agents, or should the planner be responsible for including them in files_affected?

options.label: Implicitly allow common config files
options.description: Less friction, agents will not get stuck on dependency changes

options.label: Planner must include them explicitly
options.description: Stricter, but planner template should prompt for it

decisions.question: What should be the default behavior for egg-contract request-file (escape hatch)?

options.label: Auto-approve with logging
options.description: Observability but no blocking — agents never get stuck

options.label: Queue a HITL decision for human approval
options.description: Stricter, but may slow down agents

options.label: Auto-approve by default, strict-mode flag queues HITL
options.description: Flexible: auto-approve normally, configurable strict mode

decisions.question: How should directory-sibling expansion work when a file like src/auth/login.py is in files_affected?

options.label: Shallow expansion only (dir/*)
options.description: Sibling files in same directory only

options.label: No automatic expansion
options.description: Rely on planner using globs like src/auth/*

questions.question: For test file generation: should tests/ be implicitly allowed when a source file is in files_affected, or should the planner always list test files explicitly?
Should violation counts accumulate across all pushes in a session, or reset per push? (Accumulating = second push touching out-of-scope file blocks; resetting = each push gets one free warning)

For post-agent auto-commit: should files outside the allowlist be restored silently (with a log), restored with a visible warning in the checkpoint, or treated the same as push violations (warn-then-block)?
Are there any specific common config files beyond pyproject.toml, package.json, Makefile, and tsconfig.json that should always be in the implicit allowlist?
